decisions.question: e-6192

source.question: e-6192
source.value: Calculate, in degrees to the nearest degree, the solutions to the equation $5\sin x = -7\cos x$ for $0^\circ \leq x < 360^\circ.$

decisions.reason: Observed MA content supersedes the stored value

decisions.question: e-6192

source.question: e-6192
source.value:
We divide each term of the equation by $\cos x$ and use the identity $\tan x = \dfrac{\sin x}{\cos x}.$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}5\operatorname{sin}⁡x & =-7\operatorname{cos}⁡x \\ \frac{5\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x} & =-\frac{7\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x} \\ \frac{5\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x} & =-\frac{7\cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}}{\cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}} \\ 5\cdot \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x} & =-7 \\ 5\operatorname{tan}⁡x & =-7\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we rearrange the equation and isolate $\tan x\mathbin{:}$

$$
\tan x = -\dfrac{7}{5}
$$

The length of the interval for $x$ is $2\pi$, so we will likely require $2$ solutions. 

We can immediately calculate the principal value $x\mathbin{:}$

$$
x = \arctan\left(-\dfrac{7}{5}\right) \approx -54.46
$$

This value is outside the domain $0^\circ \leq x < 360^\circ.$ To get a value that's inside the domain, we add $180^\circ\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(-\frac{7}{5})+{180}^{∘} \\  & ≈-{54.46}^{∘}+{180}^{∘} \\  & ={125.54}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

To find the other solution inside the given interval, we add $180^\circ$ to $x_1.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={x}_{1}+{180}^{∘} \\  & ≈{125.54}^{∘}+{180}^{∘} \\  & ={305.54}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

So the solutions, rounded to the nearest degree, are $x= 126^\circ, 306^\circ.$

source.question: e-6196
source.value: Calculate, in degrees to the nearest degree, the solutions to the equation $3\sin x + 12\cos x = 0$ for $-180^\circ <  x \leq 180^\circ.$

decisions.reason: Observed MA content supersedes the stored value

decisions.question: e-6196

source.question: e-6196
source.value:
We divide each term of the equation by $\cos x$ and use the identity $\tan x = \dfrac{\sin x}{\cos x}.$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}3\operatorname{sin}⁡x+12\operatorname{cos}⁡x & =0 \\ \frac{3\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}+\frac{12\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x} & =0 \\ \frac{3\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}+\frac{12\cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}}{\cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}} & =0 \\ 3\cdot \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}+12 & =0 \\ 3\operatorname{tan}⁡x+12 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we rearrange the equation and isolate $\tan x\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}3\operatorname{tan}⁡x & =-12 \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡x & =-4\end{aligned}
$$

We can immediately calculate the principal value $x\mathbin{:}$

$$
x = \arctan(-4) \approx -75.96^\circ
$$

Since this value lies inside the given domain, our first solution is $x_1 = -75.96^\circ.$

To find the other solution in the given interval, we *add* $180^\circ.$ Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={x}_{1}+{180}^{∘} \\  & ≈-{75.96}^{∘}+{180}^{∘} \\  & ={104.04}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

So the solutions, rounded to the nearest degree, are $x= -76^\circ, 104^\circ.$
